  "reasons": [
    "When a debenture of Rs 100 face value is issued at Rs 110, the excess Rs 10 represents debenture premium.",
    "Per NCERT Section 2.4.3, this amount is credited to Securities Premium Reserve Account and presented under Reserves and Surplus on the balance sheet."
  ],

  "syllabus_topic": "Issue of Debentures at Premium",

      "condition": "The excess Rs 10 charged above Rs 100 nominal value represents issue premium on debentures.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "Premium received on debentures is credited to Securities Premium Reserve Account and reported under Reserves and Surplus.",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": ["E1.1"]
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [

      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "The full issue price of Rs 110 is credited to Debentures Account as long-term debt.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "The Rs 10 premium is treated as normal operating revenue income in the Profit and Loss statement.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "The debenture transaction is treated as an issue of share capital credited under equity.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",

    }
  ],

      "option": "A",

      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The amount of premium is credited to Securities Premium Reserve account and is shown on the liabilities side of the balance sheet under the head “Reserves and Surpluses”.",
